note: SharePoint capture scope (lane P7; owner decisions 5be438765457 and 93047ba19524: the Workbench keeps what it captures in its own capture store under the Workbench state directory, and SharePointFile objects feed the documents domain). Targets: the whole QA/QC Department (QCQA) library (AOs, QA Documents such as Quality Risk Management, 02-CASES-AND-ARTIFACTS 3.1), the PLXCUSTOMERS site's 'Customer Documents' folder (its default library, resolved by site name at run time on the SHAREPOINT_SITE_ID host) the AGENTS site's '/Ontology UseCases' folder (directive 82c78b104dd6) and the Operations site's '/CM Operations Files' folder (decision 2026-10-27-case-originals-served). The first run of a root is a full walk; later runs follow the drive's change feed and a full walk repeats every full_walk_hours (and whenever the feed cannot settle a change). A root's skipped permission re-reads are bounded by permission_reread_hours: once its permission position is older, its next follow re-reads every feed entry by item id, the unchanged versions too, so a grant revoked without the sharing annotation is stale at most that bound plus the runs the re-read takes (a re-read the time budget cuts resumes past what it read; directive 1cd1c66dd47d). A walk bound (max_depth, max_folders) that is reached leaves the root incomplete with that reason, never silently whole. This file grants nothing: the capture principal still needs the live-source audience for every folder and item, and every reader is re-gated per item (path keys and item permissions recorded at capture). Read-only: nothing is ever written to SharePoint.

targets.note: The Operations site's Documents library, folder CM Operations Files: the asset tracker workbook a case brief cites (devloop/DECISIONS/2026-10-27-case-originals-served.md, Unblock). The estate scope discovers this library too (root /); this target names the folder alone.
